text:
jess-support: FYI customer BrightWorks reported negative tokens/sec and TTFT spikes in the console for dedicated-eu-1 since ~18:20 UTC. billing alarm fired. https://console.redwood.example/d/streams/brightworks

sam-oncall: looking. can you paste a permalink to the dashboard panel? which model / route?

jess-support: panel: /d/streams/ttft?orgId=1&panelId=12 route=brightworks/production small-v2 region=dedicated-eu-1. Customer says values show -350 tokens/sec and TTFT goes to -0.12s for some windows.

ravi-runtime: saw similar on internal test after a partial consumer restart earlier. zookeeper indicated a checkpoint rollback for topic=streaming-rollup-03, partition=4 at 18:17:03. probable duplicate replay wrote negative deltas when aggregator applied windowed subtraction.

maria-analytics: confirmed in clickhouse: query: 
```
SELECT window_start, sum(tokens_delta) as tokens FROM rollups
WHERE route='brightworks/production' AND window_start >= '2026-03-10 18:00'
GROUP BY window_start ORDER BY window_start LIMIT 20;
```
we see windows with tokens = -342, -1, then normal positives.

ravi-runtime: root cause idea: stream-aggregator assumes monotonic counters from producer; when replayed messages with older offsets were reprocessed after partial checkpoint drop, we applied subtraction against the newer cumulative and got negative delta.

leo-eng-sre: tagging @sam-oncall @ravi-runtime. are there consumer error logs? ops-bot: deploy/stream-aggregator/rollup-service restarted at 18:15:39 due to oom.

sam-oncall: logs from aggregator show WARN: "rollup.delta < 0" for route=brightworks/production window=2026-03-10T18:20:00Z, count=-642, trace=7f3b2c. attaching snippet:
```
2026-03-10T18:20:05Z WARN rollup-processor - route=brightworks/production partition=4 window=2026-03-10T18:20:00Z delta=-642 prev_cum=10234 new_cum=95892
```

jess-support: customer is asking if billing will be wrong. they saw negative per-second in console and invoice preview shows credit for a few minutes.

maria-analytics: billing pipeline reads tokens from backfilled hourly aggregates; negative rollups can propagate to invoice previews. we should clamp negatives ASAP and schedule backfill.

ravi-runtime: hotfix proposal: clamp negative deltas to zero at rollup ingestion and emit metric 'rollup.negative-clamp' for auditing. quick PR pushed: 7f3b2c-hotfix (rolling to canary).

sam-oncall: deployed hotfix to canary at 18:45. canary shows no new negative values for same route but historical windows still negative.

leo-eng-sre: created backfill job: scripts/fix_negative_rollups.py — it reads raw events from kafka between 18:00-19:00 and recomputes correct window sums, then writes corrected aggregates to clickhouse. running in dry-run now.

maria-analytics: running backfill dry-run shows corrected windows: previously -342 -> 1324, -1 -> 11. expected billing impact small but non-zero; will re-run invoice preview after backfill.

jess-support: customer updated: appreciate quick reply, wants ETA for invoice fix.

ravi-runtime: ETA: backfill scheduled 19:30 UTC, full write after validation ~19:50, billing preview refresh by 20:10. will notify when done.

sam-oncall: followups: 1) add a consumer checkpoint healthcheck to alert if rollback happens; 2) add assert in aggregator to ignore replays older than last-processed-cum for a partition; 3) ops runbook update for restart OOM.

leo-eng-sre: created ticket RN-3145 for checkpoints + RN-3146 for alert. added playbook steps in ops-runbook/doc.

ops-bot: backfill job started (dry-run) at 19:28:10, job_id=bf-1987.

maria-analytics: dry-run validated, writing corrections now. updating invoice preview and console panels.

ops-bot: backfill job bf-1987 write-step completed at 19:49:55, affected_windows=6, corrected_total_tokens=+18476.

jess-support: relayed ETA to customer; they are relieved. said please add a note to billing team.

sam-oncall: will notify billing and create postmortem. adding regression test to CI: simulate consumer rollback and verify aggregator clamps negatives.

leo-eng-sre: closing thread once billing confirms fix applied. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
